headline: Squeeze done: $1.01B liquidated, BTC steady $85.5K, ETFs bought $618M - no dip yet
summary: The short squeeze has run its course and left nothing on sale: at 05:48 UTC on 22 September BTC is $85,554 (day open $86,598, 69% of the way up an $81,387-$87,447 range and 2.2% below the high), ETH $2,737.20 (57% up its range) and SOL $116.97 (65% up), with all three up 9.6-14.9% on the week. About $1.01bn of positions were liquidated in 24 hours across roughly 135,000 traders, 82% of it shorts ($844m), with $608m in BTC and $181m in ETH, and CoinDesk reports the past hour's liquidations under $11m - the forced buying is over rather than accelerating. The important change since the 01:57 UTC briefing is that the leverage warning eased slightly instead of worsening: Hyperliquid open interest fell to $3.76bn on BTC (from $3.88bn) and $3.11bn on ETH (from $3.23bn), ETH's futures premium halved to 0.044% from 0.068%, and funding is flat and cheap at 0.00125%/h on all three, while the passive bid finally showed up with $618m of US spot bitcoin ETF net inflow on 21 September taking fund assets to $105.59bn. Against that the calendar is now the risk: Fed speakers today and Powell on 23 September after the 16 September hike, Xi at the White House on 24 September with the Busan truce expiring 10 November, and a $16.6bn Deribit quarterly expiry on 25 September. Mood is Greed on the composite at 69.6 but Fear & Greed is at 78, squarely Extreme Greed - an extended tape near the top of its range, not a bounce setup.

BTC.note: About $85,554, 2.2% under the $87,446.7 high and 69% of the way up the day's $81,387.1-$87,446.7 range after climbing from roughly $81,000 to a $86,980 hourly peak and drifting sideways since; Hyperliquid open interest has come off to $3.76bn from $3.88bn at 01:57 UTC with funding unchanged at 0.00125%/h and the premium steady at 0.059%, so the leverage is no longer building, but any entry here is still near the top of an eight-month high rather than into a discount, and this cycle's GDELT 24h news-tone component came back empty so the composite is running on four inputs instead of five.

ETH.note: About $2,737.20, the laggard at +2.7% on 24 hours versus BTC's +4.8%, and the weakest positioned of the three at 57% up its $2,645.66-$2,806.69 range; it printed its highest level since January and a single whale rotated 1,107 BTC (about $86.76m) into 34,422 ETH (about $86.5m) and staked all of it over five days, but one whale is not a flow - its Hyperliquid open interest fell to $3.11bn from $3.23bn and its futures premium halved to 0.044% from 0.068%, so the fresh leverage that was concentrated here at midnight has already been unwound.

SOL.note: About $116.97, +4.7% on 24 hours and the week's leader at +14.9%, sitting 2.5% below its $119.97 high and 65% up an $111.38-$119.97 range; it still carries the thinnest book at $701m of Hyperliquid open interest with funding at 0.00125%/h, which makes it the most reflexive of the three in both directions, and Alpenglow mainnet activation on 28 September - a feature-gate rollout cutting finality from about 12.8 seconds to 150 milliseconds, with Agave 4.3 recommended for general validator adoption on 21 September - is asset-specific event risk just outside the week.

drivers.title: The $1.01bn short squeeze finished, and the leverage behind it came off instead of building
drivers.detail: Roughly $1.01bn of positions were liquidated in 24 hours across about 135,000 traders, with $844m of that - 82% - shorts, $608m in BTC and $181m in ETH, and the single largest a ~$21m BTC position on Hyperliquid; past-hour liquidations have since dropped below $11m from a $300m-plus peak, leaving BTC flat above $85,000 and dogecoin leading the rebound with a 15% move. That matters more than the direction: the Hyperliquid open interest that grew into the 01:57 UTC briefing has since fallen on all three majors and ETH's futures premium halved, so the squeeze exhausted itself rather than rolling into a second leg of borrowed positioning.

drivers.title: The ETF channel turned buyer: $618m in one day, plus Strategy's first purchase in three weeks
drivers.detail: US spot bitcoin ETFs took in about $618m of net inflow on 21 September, lifting total fund assets to $105.59bn and cumulative net inflows to $55.8bn - a real change from the week to 18 September, when the whole week netted roughly $6.1m after $746.3m of midweek outflows were clawed back by a $433.03m Friday led by Fidelity's FBTC ($310.72m) and BlackRock's IBIT ($108.44m). Alongside it Strategy disclosed 950 BTC bought for $75.7m at an average $79,670, its first purchase in about three weeks, which is below today's price.

drivers.title: Fed week: speakers today, Powell tomorrow, flash PMIs Wednesday
drivers.detail: The Fed hiked 25bp on 16 September in a unanimous 12-0 vote, its first hike since 2023, and pencilled 2026 headline and core PCE at 3.7% and 3.4% against a 2% target, with four policymakers expecting two more hikes this year; central bankers make around ten appearances this week. Today brings the Richmond Fed manufacturing index at 14:00 UTC with New York's John Williams at 14:05 UTC, Vice Chair Philip Jefferson at 14:20 UTC and Richmond's Thomas Barkin at 17:00 UTC (Kiplinger's calendar also puts Powell on 23 September), then S&P Global flash PMIs on Wednesday - euro area 08:00 UTC, US 13:45 UTC - the first full-month activity read since the hike. The stored history flags this exact channel: 'inflation/CPI' headlines preceded a BTC dip within 6h 2.6% of the time versus 1.0% by chance (2.67x lift, n=117, held in both halves of the data).

drivers.title: Xi has landed in Washington; the summit is Thursday with a 100% tariff law already on the books
drivers.detail: Xi Jinping arrived in Washington for his first White House visit since 2015 and meets Trump on 24 September, with Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and USTR Jamieson Greer having held preparatory talks with Vice Premier He Lifeng in New York on 20 September; the aim is to extend the Busan trade truce before it expires on 10 November, with soybean and Boeing purchases, rare earths and AI export controls on the table. The two-sided part for risk assets is that Trump signed the Graham sanctions act on 18 September authorising tariffs of up to 100% on the largest buyers of Russian oil, China among them - a ready-made escalation path if the summit goes badly - while a clean truce extension removes a risk premium that is currently priced in.

drivers.title: Three mechanical events inside 72 hours: BitMEX closes, Deribit settles $16.6bn, XPL unlocks
drivers.detail: BitMEX - the exchange that invented the perpetual swap - shuts down on 23 September at 04:00 UTC after an eleven-year run, with deposits credited only until then and unwithdrawn balances charged 1% a year, so open positions there have to move somewhere else this week. Then on 25 September at 08:00 UTC the Deribit quarterly expiry settles about $16.6bn notional - $14.73bn of BTC across roughly 186,000 contracts and $1.92bn of ETH across about 756,100 - with max pain cited near $72,000, far below spot, and the same day brings Plasma's XPL cliff releasing 1.76-1.81bn tokens, some 63-65% of circulating supply and about $158m, plus smaller unlocks in Humanity Protocol and others. None of these is directional on its own; together they are the week's largest source of forced, non-fundamental flow.

drivers.title: With CLARITY dead, the agencies are writing the rules and the money is going political
drivers.detail: After the 49-50 Senate cloture failure killed federal market-structure legislation, SEC Chairman Paul Atkins and CFTC Chair Mike Selig have both said they are ready to ship digital-asset rules without it, building on the March 2026 SEC-CFTC joint interpretation and August's proposed 'Regulation Crypto Assets' regime; crypto super PAC Fairshake has responded by committing $30m against Sherrod Brown. Note that the market rallied 13% straight through the CLARITY defeat, so the legislative failure is not what is pricing here - the regulatory path is now an agency-rulemaking story with a multi-quarter clock, not a headline risk for this week.

watch.what: New York Fed's John Williams, then Vice Chair Philip Jefferson at 14:20 UTC and Richmond's Thomas Barkin at 17:00 UTC, with the Richmond Fed manufacturing index at 14:00 UTC. The first read on how hard the Fed leans into further hikes after the 16 September move.
BitMEX shuts down permanently. Positions and balances still there have to be moved, and the venue that invented perps leaving the market is a small liquidity event in its own right.

US S&P Global flash PMI (euro area 08:00 UTC, UK 08:30 UTC) - the first full-month activity read since the hike - alongside Powell on Kiplinger's calendar and Fed Governor Michael Barr on the Crypto Times calendar.

Trump hosts Xi at the White House on tariffs, rare earths, soybeans and AI. Two-sided: extending the Busan truce before its 10 November expiry removes a risk premium, a breakdown meets a signed law authorising up to 100% tariffs on buyers of Russian oil.
Deribit quarterly options expiry, about $16.6bn notional ($14.73bn BTC, $1.92bn ETH), max pain near $72,000. Same day: Plasma XPL cliff unlock of roughly $158m, about 63-65% of circulating supply.

Solana's Alpenglow mainnet activation, cutting finality from about 12.8 seconds to 150 milliseconds - the largest protocol change of the quarter for SOL and the main asset-specific risk among the three majors.

BEA Personal Income and Outlays with the August PCE print, the cleanest test of the Fed's 3.7% headline / 3.4% core projections. Quarter end and the SEC fiscal year end fall the same day and tend to pull flows around.

Context for any pullback that does appear, from the stored history: BTC dips during greed got +1.5% back in 7 of 7 cases, ETH in 92.9% of 28 and SOL in 93.8% of 48, with a typical extra drop after the trigger of -0.3% to -0.5% and a median time to recovery of 3.5-5.0 hours. Against that, today's market state most resembles 2025-07-10, 2025-06-10 and 2024-07-22, after which BTC's median 30-day move was -3.0% (up in 50.0% of them).
